Deilbach catchment and its rain inputs

Where the water that passes the Kupferdreh gauge comes from, which gauges see it on the way, and which rain data we plan to collect for the 48-hour forecast.

Input plan from 13 Oct 2026, shown without the forecast ring. What the forecast collects today (every second ICON-D2 point, no per-zone forecast, radar about 30 minutes after the hour) is in docs/catchment.md.

111.5 km² drain to Kupferdreh 5 zones, split at the gauges 119 radar cells (1 km) 36 forecast grid points (2.2 km)

How to read the map

  • The thick dark outline is the catchment (Einzugsgebiet): every drop of rain that falls inside it ends up flowing past Kupferdreh.
  • The coloured areas are five zones. Each zone ends at a gauge, so rain on a zone shows up at that gauge before it reaches Kupferdreh. The red zone ends at Kupferdreh itself.
  • Squares are river gauges, triangles are rain gauges, small dots are the points where the weather model ICON-D2 calculates rain.
  • Hover any symbol or zone for details. Use the switches to hide layers.

The five zones

Rain on a zone reaches Kupferdreh along a different path. Upper zones pass a gauge first, so we see their water coming hours ahead. Zones without a gauge give no such warning; for them, rain data is the only early signal.

NevigesHardenberger Bach above the Neviges gauge
20.4 km²21 radar cells8 forecast points

Passes the Neviges gauge, then Langenberg 2. The longest way to Kupferdreh, so the earliest warning.

Upper DeilbachDeilbach above Langenberg 2, without Neviges
37.9 km²41 radar cells12 forecast points

The largest zone. Its water passes Langenberg 2 before it reaches Kupferdreh.

FelderbachFelderbach above the Nierenhof gauge
22.6 km²25 radar cells7 forecast points

Passes Nierenhof, then joins the Deilbach just above Grenzweg.

MiddleBetween Langenberg 2 / Nierenhof and Grenzweg
12.5 km²14 radar cells3 forecast points

Only the BRW gauge Grenzweg sees this water. Until BRW agrees, it has no gauge we can use, like the lower zone.

LowerBelow Grenzweg down to Kupferdreh
18.2 km²18 radar cells6 forecast points

No gauge upstream of Kupferdreh. Rain here raises the level fastest, and radar is the only early signal.

Two kinds of rain data

Observed rain

What has already fallen. Comes from weather radar (DWD RADOLAN), which measures rain every kilometre and is corrected with rain gauges each hour. It tells the model about water that is on its way but has not reached any gauge yet, and how wet the ground already is.

Available about 25 minutes after the hour, with history back to 2005.

Rain forecast

What will fall in the next 48 hours. Comes from DWD's weather model ICON-D2, which runs every 3 hours on a 2.2 km grid. We read it through Open-Meteo, which also keeps old forecasts, so the model can learn from forecasts exactly as they were issued.

Archive of past forecasts from February 2024.

One value per input, or several?

Observed rain: one value per zone. The radar sees each square kilometre, so each zone's average is built from 14 to 41 radar cells and is a real measurement. The zones differ in how quickly their water arrives and whether a gauge sees it first, which is exactly what the model needs. We add one more value, the wettest single cell, so a short, heavy shower is not averaged away.

Rain forecast: one average plus one "high" value. The weather model often puts a shower 10 to 30 km from where it actually falls, more than the size of any zone. Splitting the forecast by zone would mostly add noise. So we keep the average over the catchment, plus a high value (90th percentile) over the catchment and 10 km around it, which warns when a storm is forecast nearby. We still store the per-zone values, because they cost nothing and let us test this assumption.

Every hourly run stores the forecast it can see at that moment, with the model's own run time. Training then uses only what was known when each forecast was made. Forecast points per zone: Neviges 8, Upper Deilbach 12, Felderbach 7, Middle 3, Lower 6.

Terms

Catchment (Einzugsgebiet)
The land area that drains to one point of a river. Here: everything that drains to the Kupferdreh gauge.
Zone
Our own split of the catchment at the gauges, so rain can be matched to the gauge that sees it first.
RADOLAN RW
DWD's hourly rain map from weather radar, corrected with rain gauges. One value per square kilometre for all of Germany.
ICON-D2
DWD's high-resolution weather model for Germany. Runs every 3 hours, forecasts 48 hours ahead on a 2.2 km grid.
Open-Meteo
A free weather API (non-commercial use) that serves ICON-D2 as simple data and keeps past forecasts.
Lead time
How far ahead a forecast value is, for example +6 h. Forecasts get less reliable with lead time.
Issue time
When a forecast was made. The model may only use data that existed at that moment.
90th percentile
The value that 9 out of 10 grid points stay below. A robust "high" value that one odd point cannot dominate.
LANUV, BRW, DWD
NRW's environment agency, the regional water board in Haan, and Germany's national weather service.
Built 13 Oct 2026 from GSK3E (NRW, edition 2019), the RADOLAN grid definition, the ICON-D2 regular grid (0.02°), OpenHygon NRW and DWD station lists.
